description.narrative: The development objective of Tourism Development Project is to improve the performance of tourism in targeted destinations in Ghana. This project has four components. 1) The first component, Strengthening the tourism enabling environment, aims to address the following constraints most likely to have transformative impact on the tourism sector in Ghana: training and skills development of the industry, aviation and entry visa policy, and branding and marketing. 2) The second component, Developing tourism sites and destinations, seeks to diversify the leisure tourism offering in Ghana by identifying and upgrading the most promising destination areas. 3) The third component, Tourism enterprise support program, aims to finance the costs of tourism enterprise matching grants and business development services training. Qualified enterprises will be invited to submit proposals that will be evaluated for viability. 4) The fourth component, Project management and institutional strengthening, aims to provide support to Ministry of Tourism, Arts and Culture (MoTAC) to manage and coordinate the project.
The project development objective is to improve the performance of tourism in targeted destinations in Ghana

condition.narrative: Financing Agreement, Schedule 2, Section I, A.2 (a): Without limitation upon the provisions of paragraph 1 of this Section I.A, theRecipient shall no later than three (3) months after the Effectiveness Date establish and thereafter maintain throughout Projectimplementation, a National Steering Committee (“NSC”) with a composition, mandate, terms of reference and resources satisfactory tothe Association. The NSC shall be chaired by the Minister of MoTAC or a designated representative, and shall include, inter alia,representative of MoFARI, MoF, MoI, MoA, MoLNR, MoTI and at least two representatives from the financial sector and private sector

Financing Agreement, Schedule 2, Section I, A.3 (a): The Recipient through MoTAC shall not later than three (3) months from theEffectiveness Date, establish and thereafter maintain throughout project implementation, a Project technical committee (ProjectTechnical Committee or PTC) comprising of the Participating Agencies and chaired by the Chief Director, responsible for resolutionof technical and implementation challenges

Financing Agreement, Schedule 2, Section IV, A.1: Except as the Recipient and the Association shall otherwise agree, the Recipientthrough MoTAC shall: (a) not later than six (6) months from the Signature Date open an account in Ghana Cedis (“Escrow Account”)forthe Project, in the Bank of Ghana on terms and conditions satisfactory to the Association; (b) deposit into said Escrow Account:(i) an initial amount equivalent to a hundred thousand Dollars ($100,000); and (ii) thereafter, deposit on annual basis throughoutProject implementation an amount equivalent to a hundred thousand Dollars ($100,000); and (c) ensure that funds deposited into theEscrow Account in accordance with paragraph (b) of this Section shall be used exclusively to finance expenditures in connectionwith potential Resettlement Compensation which might arise as a result of implementing the civil works under Part B.1 (b) of theProject.

title.narrative: Annual growth rates in international tourists at targeted attraction sites

comment.narrative: This indicator target was revised downwards when the project was restructured in June 2022 due to COVID-19-related lockdowns and travel restrictions. At that time, international tourist arrivals had significantly declined with very little sign of revival. However, the PDO indicator end target of 3.0% (i.e., 56,613 visits in 2022) was astronomically surpassed, reaching 43.3% (i.e., 81,113 visits by the end of 2023). This significant increase is due to a resurgence in Ghana's tourism sector, with the biggest contributions coming during the holiday season and festivities in December 2023.

title.narrative: Number of international arrivals identifying tourism as their main purpose of visit

comment.narrative: Visitors whose primary purpose of visit is tourism, as defined by UNWTO, are included in this data. This PDO indicator reached and surpassed its end target of 744,891, achieving 1,078,963 international arrivals. This was primarily due to the strong resilience and resurgence of the tourism sector following the lifting of COVID-19-related bans on travel and international flights.

title.narrative: Number of accredited tourism and hospitality training centers

comment.narrative: Accredited by systems developed through the project, this intermediate-level indicator (building of a PPP school) will not be achieved at project closure. This is because MOTAC could not complete the entire PPP assignment, which included feasibility and transaction advisory, due to time constraints and the imminent project closure. Furthermore, given the current macro-fiscal crisis, it is unlikely that funding will be made available for this activity in the near term. As a result, the PPP advisory contract was downgraded to a feasibility study. CPCS, the contractor for this assignment, advised the government on the option of housing the tourism training within one (or two) of the universities in the country until such time that construction funds are made available by the government.Â

title.narrative: Private enterprises receiving matching grants of which 50 percent are women owned or managed

comment.narrative: This IRI measures the number of private enterprises receiving matching grants, including those that are women-owned or managed. The indicator's end target of 200 was reached and substantially surpassed, with 1,249 enterprises benefiting due to the reallocation of funds to grants following the restructuring in June 2022. Similarly, the end target of 50% for women-owned or managed enterprises was surpassed, with 55% (687) of the supported enterprises being women-owned or managed.
